title: AES-256-CBC encryption/decryption utility for sensitive fields
description: Create a reusable encryption utility using Node.js crypto module with AES-256-CBC to encrypt and decrypt sensitive values like AI API keys and GitHub access tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: encrypt(plaintext: string): string function returns base64-encoded IV + ciphertext
decrypt(ciphertext: string): string function recovers original plaintext
Uses ENCRYPTION_KEY from environment (must be exactly 32 characters)
Different calls to encrypt(x) produce different output (random IV)

steps.details: Create server/src/utils/encryption.ts. Use Node.js built-in crypto module. const ALGORITHM = 'aes-256-cbc'. const KEY = Buffer.from(process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY!, 'utf8') — assert length is 32. export function encrypt(plaintext: string): string: 1) const iv = crypto.randomBytes(16). 2) const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv(ALGORITHM, KEY, iv). 3) const encrypted = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(plaintext), cipher.final()]). 4) Return iv.toString('hex') + ':' + encrypted.toString('hex'). export function decrypt(ciphertext: string): string: 1) Split on ':'. 2) const iv = Buffer.from(parts[0], 'hex'). 3) const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv(ALGORITHM, KEY, iv). 4) Return decipher.update + final as utf8.
encrypt('my-api-key') — verify output is different each call (random IV). decrypt(encrypt('my-api-key')) — verify returns 'my-api-key'. Try with 100-char string — verify round-trip works.

technicalNotes: ENCRYPTION_KEY must be exactly 32 bytes for AES-256. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 16 (gives 32 hex chars = 16 bytes) — NO, use openssl rand -base64 24 | head -c 32 or crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex').slice(0,32)
Store IV prepended to ciphertext so each encrypted value is self-contained
Use the Node.js built-in crypto — no external dependency needed
